body:
Quiet day — no arbitrage found. The scanner returned zero opportunities across both platforms today, and that's a legitimate, unremarkable result rather than a gap in coverage. Kalshi's Sept-30-2026 and year-end gold above $X settlement ladder and Polymarket's touch-price contracts on XAUUSD are pricing consistently with each other: the $4,400-and-above year-end strike sits near a coin-flip (bid 0.58 / ask 0.60), and Polymarket's hit $4,500 in September touch contract trades around 0.77-0.79, both broadly in line with spot gold trading in the mid-$4,400s right now. Gold has been unusually volatile lately — it hit an all-time record above $5,600/oz in late January 2026, then pulled back sharply, and was recently reported falling toward roughly $4,430 after a stronger-than-expected US jobs report pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher, so the current $4,400-4,500 range reflects a real retracement, not a data error.

The one thing worth flagging for readers, not as an edge but as a caveat: several of the far-out-of-the-money Kalshi strikes (e.g., above $4,930.99, above $5,010.99) show zero 24-hour volume, and a number of Polymarket's weekly touch contracts (the week of September 7 series) have bid/ask spreads as wide as $0.01/$0.99. Those are classic thin-book quotes — a single resting order at the edge of the book, not a tradable market — and any apparent mispricing there is a liquidity artifact rather than a capturable arbitrage.

Bottom line: prices across Kalshi and Polymarket's gold contracts are internally consistent with each other and with the reported spot price near $4,400-4,470, and the scanner found nothing actionable. No trades, no positioning — just a market pausing after a historic run.
headline: Gold prediction markets show no arbitrage as Kalshi, Polymarket prices align near spot
